item.title: v5.16.3
item.description: • Fix: since v5.16.0, the Chrome converter never became ready when Chrome needed more than 5 seconds to start (e.g. many fonts on a slow disk). Chrome was killed and restarted every 10 seconds, endlessly. New option chromeStartTimeout ( CARBONE_CHROME_START_TIMEOUT , "chromeStartTimeout" in config.json ): maximum time in milliseconds for Chrome to start and be ready to convert. 60 seconds by default, 0 = no limit. When this limit is reached, the log line WARNING: Chrome factory N is not ready after X ms (chromeStartTimeout). Chrome is restarted. is printed.

item.title: v5.16.1
item.description: • [EE] Fix: when the job balancer is enabled ( CARBONE_JOB_BALANCER=true ), the result of a job executed by another peer could be lost if the connection between the two peers was cut for a few seconds. The report generation then waited until its timeout and failed. It happened mostly with large reports (hundreds of :appendTemplate for example), which keep a peer busy for several seconds. A connection between peers is now closed after 3 heartbeats without answer ( 3 Ã peerCheckInterval , 30 to 40 seconds by default) instead of 1 (10 to 20 seconds). A busy peer is no longer disconnected. A peer which is really down is detected after 30 to 40 seconds instead of 10 to 20 seconds. If the peer which sent the job is disconnected when the result is ready, the result is sent again every peerCheckInterval / 2 (5 seconds by default) until this peer reconnects, during the timeout of the job (5 minutes at most). New log lines: PEER RESPONSE job=... to=... postponed: peer disconnected when the first attempt fails, and PEER RESPONSE job=... to=... lost: the peer did not reconnect in time when the peer did not come back.

item.title: v5.16.0
item.description:
• â ï¸ [On-Premise] Security: the default securityLevel is now set to 1084 instead of 0 . It activates: 4 : disable the useless features of LibreOffice (crash reports, automatic font/extension installation...) 8 : disable the execution of scripts and macros in LibreOffice 16 : LibreOffice does not use external links (images...) of documents 32 : LibreOffice refuses exotic file formats 1024 : block outgoing traffic (images, :attachFile , :appendFile , Chrome resources, webhooks...) to a local network ( 127.x , 10.x , 172.16-31.x , 192.168.x , 169.254.x , localhost , ...). When the request leaves directly, the IP addresses returned by the DNS are checked too (DNS rebinding). A hostname refused because it resolves to a local address returns the same error as a hostname which does not exist ( ENOTFOUND ), so internal DNS names cannot be discovered. Start Carbone with DEBUG=carbone:egress to print the real reason. To restore the previous behavior, use --securityLevel 0 , CARBONE_SECURITY_LEVEL=0 or "securityLevel": 0 in config.json .
• â¡ï¸ Improved Carbone ICE (Instant Converter Engine) . PDFs are closer to Word and LibreOffice. Word (DOCX): A document with tracked changes shows the current version: old formatting is ignored, moved text is written once, and deleted text no longer leaves tabs, line breaks or pictures. Tables exported from Google Docs stay on the page. Page numbers written by Google Docs are displayed, with the font of the text around them. A footer that showed "Page sur 2" now shows "Page 1 sur 2". A document without default styles is laid out like Word: Aptos 12, the usual space under each paragraph, and table cells without inner margin. A picture raised or lowered beside the text sits at the height of its line. A heading kept with the next paragraph stays on the page when only a little space is missing at the bottom. Numbered headings and the entries of a table of contents (title and page number) follow Word. LibreOffice (ODT): Icons, badges… (read more: https://carbone.io/changelog.html#v5-16-0)

item.title: v5.15.5
item.description: • Fix: Carbone no longer crashes with the error ERR_STREAM_UNABLE_TO_PIPE when an HTTP client closes the connection before receiving its file ( POST /render/:templateId?download=true , GET /render/:renderId and GET /template/:templateId ).

item.title: v5.15.4
item.description: • Fix: DOCX templates using :html(inline) in a paragraph with borders or tab stops no longer fail with the error Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'type') .

item.title: v5.15.3
item.description:
• Fix: When converting HTML to PDF using Chrome, images could stop downloading after processing a web page that changed the Content-Security-Policy (CSP).
• Improved Carbone ICE (Instant Converter Engine), especially for DOCX to PDF conversions: If table of contents are saved with only first-level entries (common in Carbone templates), it is now rebuilt like Word does: deeper entries receive the correct styles and indentation. If a paragraph specifies a style not defined in the document, it now uses the default style instead. Page breaks: If the first paragraph inside a content control starts with a page break, any extra space above is removed on the new page, just like Word does. Charts: For charts with multiple data series and no title set, Word's default title ("Chart Title", in the document's language) is now displayed instead of leaving the space empty. Titles coming from spreadsheet cells are also shown correctly. Lines mixing fonts: If a line has both a body font and a marker font (like Symbol or Wingdings), the line height now matches Word: it uses the tallest font's ascent and the deepest descent. Improved ODT to PDF conversion: For bullet lists where the bullet uses a different font or size than the text, the line height now matches LibreOffice (highest ascent and deepest descent), and the text sits on the same baseline as the bullet.

item.title: v5.15.2
item.description:
• :appendTemplate is much faster when it is called many times with a large data-set: each sub-document no longer receives a copy of the data. They are copied only if the appended template modifies them with the :set formatter. The jsonSize statistic sent to the afterRender storage plugin is now always 0 for "child" renders, as their data is already counted in the jsonSize of the parent render.
• Fix: The :set formatter now accepts whitespace around its name and parameter, like {d.value : set ( d.other.sub ) } . Previously, this syntax was not recognized as a :set marker: the value was stored with the legacy behavior (only at the root level of d or c , and only available to the tags placed after it in the document).

item.title: v5.15.1
item.description:
• Improved Carbone ICE (Instant Converter Engine) for DOCX-to-PDF conversions: Table of contents now supports heading numbers before entries (if present) Headings with no color set are now white or black, depending on the background shade. Numbered heading shading now covers the number too. Conditional formatting for a tableâs first/last row or column also applies to list items inside cells, not just plain paragraphs. Section pages are now laid out with the correct header. Previously, a sectionâs first page could be pushed down by a taller header from later pages, moving content down by up to 10 points.
• [On-Premise] Improved and fixed the statistics sent to the afterRender storage plugin: Added a new type field: "sync" : for a synchronously generated document, "async" : for documents generated asynchronously and queued using the carbone-webhook-url header, "child" : for sub-documents generated by the appendTemplate formatter. Fix: Batch rendering (using batchSplitBy ) previously sent no metrics; the metrics object was missing and "isDebugActive": true did not provide a debug object. The batchSize now counts all generated documents, so for a batch of 50 documents, "batchSize": 50" is returned. Fix: The jsonSize statistic was always missing for asynchronously generated documents Fix: Improved error handling for batch generation if a batch reaches the time limit, a timeout error is now correctly returned.

item.title: v5.15.0
item.description:
• Added the failOn option of POST /render : with "failOn": ["IMAGE_URL_ERROR"] , the report generation stops and returns an error if an image cannot be downloaded from its URL, instead of replacing it with the "broken image" placeholder. As with :appendFile and :appendTemplate , an empty or undefined image value is not an error, and the report is generated as usual. Only images coming from a URL are concerned: base64 images, barcodes and charts keep their current behavior. The option must be an array of strings, and an unknown value is rejected with an explicit error instead of being ignored.
• â¡ï¸ Improved Carbone ICE (Instant Converter Engine) , even faster than the first version in 5.14.0, still requires no LibreOffice or any other program on the machine. Use it the same way: "converter": "I" in the options of POST /render , or "Carbone ICE" in the document converter panel of the Studio preview, or with {o.converter=I} in the template. Improved DOCX to PDF conversion : Table of contents: entries and their page numbers are automatically updated. Footnotes: now show their separator and notes Fixes more than 100 bugs: Rows taller than a page, page break before, section-specific page numbering, vertical text, shape groups, text in shapes and columns, floating tables, cell and header row heights, cell clipping, table borders, whitespace around text, and the positioning of shapes and images, complex sections, etc... Supports ODT to PDF conversion [Beta] From 3x to 300x faster than the LibreOffice converter, with speed improvements scaling with document size (the larger the document, the greater the speed gain). Supports ODT templates with different page formats and sections (paper size, margins, headers/footers, mixed portrait/landscape, text columns), paragraph and character styles, right-to-left languages, lists and outline numbering, tables (borders, shading, merges, floating tables, rows kept together), images, shapes with text inside them, connectors,… (read more: https://carbone.io/changelog.html#v5-15-0)

item.title: v5.14.4
item.description: • â ï¸ Important Security Update: Following an in-depth internal penetration test, we strongly recommend updating to this version to address two critical security fixes and numerous other improvements that significantly increase Carbone's overall security. Contact us if you want more details about the two critical security issues. The release note remains intentionally vague for security reasons, and the Open Source version will be updated in a few weeks. Critical: The LibreOffice converter is now significantly more secure. Critical: For historical reasons, Carbone allowed changing the template file extension (file type) via the API without strict validation. This is now restricted: only recognized formats (like docx , xlsx , xhtml , etc.) are accepted. LibreOffice converter: watermarking, file attachments ( :appendFile , :attachFile , :appendTemplate ), and signing ( :sign ) now work together even when generating password-protected PDFs. Previously, as soon as a PDF was protected with a password, the other features would stop working. Carbone ICE (Instant Converter Engine) now supports PDF encryption and watermarks, with the same options as Chrome, OnlyOffice, and LibreOffice. Documents generated in HTML, XHTML, SVG, or XML are now served with the Content-Security-Policy: sandbox HTTP header. This causes browsers to give these files an isolated origin and blocks all scripts, protecting against code injection. The X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header is now reliably set on every response. Browsers are required to respect the Content-Type Carbone provides, reducing the risk of content-type based attacks. Added securityLevel options to remove local references in generated documents for these formats: docx , xlsx , xlsm , pptx , odt , ods , odp , odg , fodt , fods , fodp , html , xhtml , md , svg , xml , txt , css , rtf , mht , mhtml , vml . SECURITY_API_REMOVE_LOCAL_HYPERLINK (256): Removes hyperlinks and references to private networks (local IPs, localhost,… (read more: https://carbone.io/changelog.html#v5-14-4)

item.title: v5.14.3
item.description: • Fix: a template error in a batch item (e.g. Missing showEnd or hideEnd ) no longer crashes the worker. The error is now returned to the callback instead.

item.title: v5.14.2
item.description:
• Fix: Version v5.14.0 introduced a regression due to a security headers update, which prevented downloading generated documents inside an iframe. This has been fixed.
• Fix: HEAD /render/:renderId is now allowed without authentication, like GET /render/:renderId . A HEAD used to return 401 when authentication was on.

item.title: v5.14.1
item.description:
• [EE] Fix: :set() with a relative path (e.g. {d.obj.val:set(.flag)} ) no longer crashes when the parent object is missing from the data. The value is left unset, the same way a marker naming missing data prints nothing.
• [EE] Fix: batchReportName is now respected even when the ZIP contains only one file.
• Carbone ICE (Instant Converter Engine): now correctly handles line breaks.

item.title: v5.14.0
item.description:
• Upgraded all dependencies and switched from Node 22 to Node 24
• â¡ï¸ New converter: Carbone ICE (Instant Converter Engine) . It reads a DOCX and converts it to PDF directly within Carbone, without relying on LibreOffice, OnlyOffice, Chrome or any other program on the machine. There is no office suite to install, no external process to start, watch or restart, and no temporary file written between the report generation and its conversion. Up to 60x faster than LibreOffice on a 1000-page DOCX, and 3x faster on a one-page document. The bigger the document, the wider the gap: a large report no longer pays the fixed cost of an office suite loading it, laying it out and printing it. When the job balancer is off, the document is handed directly from the render process to the converter in memory. On a 150-page report, this reduces the handover time to 30 ms instead of 345 ms. How to use it : pass "converter": "I" in the options of POST /render , next to the existing "L" (LibreOffice), "O" (OnlyOffice) and "C" (Chrome). In the Studio, pick "Carbone ICE (docx to pdf)" in the document converter panel of the preview. The converter is enabled and available by default. It can be disabled by setting carboneIcePath (environment variable CARBONE_CARBONE_ICE_PATH ) to an empty string. Multi-threaded : Carbone ICE converts multiple documents in parallel, controlled by the factories setting ( CARBONE_FACTORIES ). Each factory runs as a worker thread. Scope for this first release: DOCX to PDF conversion only. Support for more formats coming soon. Pages/sections: Handles page size/orientation, section margins, headers, footers, mixed portrait/landscape, page/section breaks, text columns. Headers/footers: Different headers/footers for first, odd/even pages, per section. Calculates PAGE , NUMPAGES , SECTIONPAGES . Paragraphs: Supports all paragraph styles, alignment (left/center/right/justified), indentation, spacing, line spacing, tab stops, borders, shading, widow/orphan… (read more: https://carbone.io/changelog.html#v5-14-0)

item.title: v5.13.1
item.description:
• â ï¸ Chrome converter Only (HTML to PDF) : Fixed a rare issue where PDFs could mix content from different reports if several were generated at the same time. Now, each PDF always contains the correct data. No more blocked or mixed documents if a download is cancelled or the connection is lost during PDF creation. Errors or interruptions for one PDF can no longer affect another.
• [EE] Hardened the job balancer (only when CARBONE_JOB_BALANCER=true) with improved cluster-wide ID safety to prevent collisions. Cancelled or interrupted reports are now safely re-queued and are never lost or duplicated. This improvement is independent of the Chrome issue above and was made at the same time as a comprehensive review of the job system's robustness.

item.title: v5.13.0
item.description:
• Chrome converter improvements: Reverted the changes in 5.12.0 regarding the maximum message size between Carbone and Chrome. Chrome enforces a built-in 100MB limit on messages (input HTML, or generated PDF), regardless of what Carbone sets for its WebSocket. The Carbone-defined limit is therefore removed. When the Chrome limit is reached, Carbone now swiftly restores communication, ensuring stability. Carbone forces Chrome to exit after 5 seconds if it cannot shut down properly, preventing an infinite wait.
• Added the ability to disable detection of missing i+1 tag in v5 when a pre-release tag ( preReleaseFeatureIn ) is set to a value lower than 5000000 in the template, API, or global configuration ( CARBONE_PRE_RELEASE_FEATURE_IN ). This can force Carbone v5 to behave like Carbone v4, helping you migrate to production without fixing legacy templates that contain syntax errors but previously worked in v4. Only features and fixes introduced up to the specified tag are enabled. Any introduced in a higher tag are disabled.
• Multiple improvements to PDF operations when generating PDFs with Chrome and OnlyOffice converters: Default encryption is now AES-256 instead of the deprecated 128-bit encryption. Password protection now encrypts document properties (Title, Author, Subject, and other Info strings). Encryption performance improved by a factor of 5.
• Appending, merging, and adding multiple watermarks to PDFs is now at least twice as fast.
• Studio improvements studio.setConfig({ defaultDataPanel : 'editor' }) selects the panel shown at startup in the data editor: 'editor' for the raw JSON editor (default), 'viewer' for the simplified JSON viewer, where clicking a property inserts the corresponding Carbone tag. The user can still switch panels with the two buttons of the data editor. Accept more template origins: Salesforce (origin = 2), Odoo (3), HubSpot (4). For reference: 0 = API, 1 = Studio.
• [EE] Markdown templates now support dynamic… (read more: https://carbone.io/changelog.html#v5-13-0)

item.title: v5.12.0
item.description:
• Improved logging: Suppressed unnecessary error messages during routine cleanup of the template/render directories when files are already deleted or removed due to race conditions.
• [EE] Cluster peer connections ( peerPort / peerEndpoints ) are now more reliable, key improvements: A periodic supervisor: Recreates the WebSocket server if it crashes or the port becomes unavailable ( EADDRINUSE ). Re-resolves peerEndpoints via DNS, so peers with changed IPs (e.g. during Kubernetes rolling updates) are rediscovered. Reconnects to any missing peer endpoint. Cleans up dead connections using a liveness timer when a connection opens, preventing rare deadlocks that could occur in previous versions and ensuring automatic connection recovery without requiring a restart. New exposed parameter peerCheckInterval (or CARBONE_PEER_CHECK_INTERVAL , default 10s): period of the peer liveness ping. The supervisor runs twice as often (half this value) so a lost peer is re-dialed faster than it is detected. Connections establish more reliably, no matter which peer initiates Supervisor uses exponential backoff: starts at half peerCheckInterval , increases up to 1 minute, and resets to fast on important events (startup, server restart, peer connect/disconnect). Peer DNS resolution is fault-tolerant: if a peer name cannot be resolved (e.g. missing DNS during a rolling update), other available peers still connect; the whole cluster isn't skipped. Maximum WebSocket message size for cluster peer connections now uses the existing maxDataSize ( CARBONE_MAX_DATA_SIZE ) parameter. By consequence, the default changed from 100MB to 60MB. Improved Event-bus logs: cluster events show peer count and addresses resolved by DNS resolution (only when changed). Unreachable peers are logged with the next retry delay (e.g. cannot reach peer ... - retrying in Xs ) at every attempt, so network issues are visible without enabling debug logs. Remaining low-level socket errors are shown only at debug… (read more: https://carbone.io/changelog.html#v5-12-0)

item.title: v5.11.0
v5.10.0-beta
item.description:
• [EE] The job balancer now also distributes asynchronous rendering jobs ( POST /render with a webhook). When enabled, both job types (document conversions and asynchronous document generations) can be offloaded to other peers that have available resources.
• Asynchronous jobs are now stored on disk in a compressed format, reducing disk usage and speeding up job transfers between peers.

item.title: v5.9.2
item.description: • Improved logs when the job balancer is used, making it easier to distinguish between external requests and internal job distribution.

item.title: v5.9.1
item.description:
• [EE] Added a job balancer (Beta) that spreads document conversion load across the peers of a cluster. When a peer is idle and another peer is overloaded, the idle peer automatically "steals" pending conversion jobs from the busy peer, runs them locally, and sends the result back. This smooths out conversion spikes without any external load balancer. Disabled by default. Enable it with the jobBalancer parameter (env var CARBONE_JOB_BALANCER=true ). It only works when the internal cluster channel is enabled, i.e. when peerPort is set (and peers are reachable through peerEndpoints ). If peerPort is not defined, the job balancer stays inactive even when jobBalancer is true . How it works: each peer periodically broadcasts the size of its conversion queue to the other peers. A peer that has free conversion factories pulls jobs from the most overloaded peer (pull-based model, so newly started peers naturally take their share and slow peers take fewer jobs). Aborted jobs and timeouts are propagated to the remote peer, and a peer stops stealing new jobs as soon as it begins a graceful shutdown. â ï¸ Like the rest of the cluster channel, this internal traffic is not authenticated or encrypted : use it only inside a secure private network.
• [EE] The OpenMetrics /metrics endpoint now exposes a new gauge carbone_reports_inflight{stage="conversion"} reporting the number of document conversion jobs currently waiting in the queue.

item.title: v5.9.0
item.description:
• If data is undefined when calling POST /render , Carbone only converts the file and skips the entire templating process. As a result, tags remain unchanged in the converted document.
• Added support for the custom header carbone-egress-header-authorization to customize the authorization header for egress traffic, such as webhooks, images, and external PDF URLs. For example, if carbone-egress-header-authorization: my-secret is included during report generation, the header authorization: my-secret will be added when Carbone calls a webhook, an external image URL, an external PDF URL, etc. If carbone-webhook-header-authorization is used at the same time, it overrides carbone-egress-header-authorization for webhook calls only. Only the authorization header can be customized, and its value must not exceed 512 characters.
• Studio: General UX improvements: Rename the "Stop Auto-Upload" button to the less technical "Finish Editing" . Improve filename readability for long filenames by displaying as much of the name as possible while always keeping the end of the filename visible (use an ellipsis in the middle). Clearly indicate that the Studio is listening for file changes with a subtle, low-resource animated icon. Clearly show how long ago the file was updated and when the latest changes were synchronized and taken into account by the Studio. Add a Docs button with an enriched menu. Fix the Profile button on Safari. Improve text search in the JSON editor with Next and Previous buttons, a result counter, and the current search position. If more than 200 occurrences are found, the UI stops counting them to avoid performance issues with very large JSON files.

item.title: v5.8.0
item.description:
• [Studio] Fix the drop-down list bug and the recent list issue in Safari.
• [On-Premise only] In Markdown templates, the special tag {o.styleSource = templateOrVersionId} allows applying the style from another DOCX or ODT template. The style template can include Carbone tags. Styles such as headings, tables, headers, and footers are applied only when converting Markdown to DOCX, ODT, or PDF.
• [EE] PDFs generated with Chrome and OnlyOffice converters now support full encryption and security options, matching LibreOffice. All PDF security features are supported: EncryptFile (boolean): Enable PDF encryption (requires password). DocumentOpenPassword (string): Password required to open the PDF. RestrictPermissions (boolean): Restrict actions like printing, copying, and editing (requires PermissionPassword ). PermissionPassword (string): Password to set/change permissions. Changes (integer): Control what edits are allowed (0: none, 1: pages, 2: forms, 3: comments/forms, 4: all except extraction). EnableCopyingOfContent (boolean): Allow content copying. EnableTextAccessForAccessibilityTools (boolean): Allow access for accessibility tools. Printing (integer): Allow printing (0: none, 1: low-res, 2: high-res).
• Increased the allowed memory allocation to 8 GB to support large XLSX reports.

item.title: v5.7.0
item.description:
• [Studio] Small UI fixes and update BeerCSS to v4.0.21 (Material Design M3) Template list: remove empty items from category/tag filters The selected item in the list is now visible only after pressing a keyboard arrow key to avoid confusion with mouse hover Replace HTML main tags with div elements to keep a single global main element and avoid bugs with the new BeerCSS Harmonize margins and button styles Use the new split buttons Improve table responsiveness
• Accept equality filters that do not strictly match types in array search expressions ( lookup ), added in v5.2.0. For example: table[rank=3] matches both rank = 3 and rank = '3' . This change aligns the behavior with the historical behavior of array filters.
